arxiv-2011-09478.creator: Hector Gisbert, Marcel Golz, Dominik Stefan Mitzel
arxiv-2011-09478.description: Abstract Rare charm decays offer the unique possibility to explore flavor-changing neutral-currents in the up-sector within the Standard Model and beyond. Due to the lack of effective methods to reliably describe its low energy dynamics, rare charm decays have been considered as less promising for long.

arxiv-2105-04710.title: Collision Between Molecular Clouds-III: The effects of cloud initial density profile on head-on collisions 2020 Collision Between Molecular Clouds-III: The effects of cloud initial density profile on head-on collisions – References
arxiv-2105-04710.creator: Tabassum S Tanvir, James E Dale
arxiv-2105-04710.description: Abstract In this third paper in our cloud-collision series, we present the results from simulations of head–on collisions with a strongly centrally–condensed initial density profile of ρ ∝ R − 2 \rm\rho\propto R^{-2} . We investigate the impact of these density profiles on the overall evolution of the simulations: the structures formed, their dynamical evolution, and their star formation activity.

arxiv-2108-05345.title: The Lawson-Hanson Algorithm with Deviation Maximization: Finite Convergence and Sparse Recovery
arxiv-2108-05345.creator: Monica Dessole, Marco Dell’Orto, Fabio Marcuzzi
arxiv-2108-05345.description: Abstract In this work we devise a new version of the Lawson-Hanson with Deviation Maximization (LHDM) algorithm, a block method for the solution of NonNegative Least Squares (NNLS). It is shown that the new algorithm here presented convergences in a finite number of steps under suitable conditions.

arxiv-2112-14085.title: Longitudinal phase-space matching between radio-frequency systems with different harmonic numbers and accelerating voltages
arxiv-2112-14085.creator: V. Ziemann, FREIA, Uppsala University
arxiv-2112-14085.description: Abstract We describe a simple mechanism to transform bunches with matched longitudinal phase-space distributions from one RF system to a matched distribution of a second RF system operating on a different harmonic and with a different accelerating voltage. The process is reversible and the longitudinal emittance is preserved. Simple equations that characterize the procedure are given and applications are discussed.

arxiv-2201-12945.title: Higher regularity of homeomorphisms in the Hartman-Grobman theorem and a conjecture on its sharpness This paper was jointly supported from the National Natural Science Foundation of China under Grant (No. 11931016 and 11671176) and Grant Fondecyt 1170466.
arxiv-2201-12945.creator: Weijie Lu Manuel Pinto Y-H Xia
arxiv-2201-12945.description: Abstract Hartman-Grobman theorem states that there is a homeomorphism H H sending the solutions of the nonlinear system onto those of its linearization under suitable assumptions. Many mathematicians have made contributions to prove Hölder continuity of the homeomorphisms. However, is it possible to improve the Hölder continuity to Lipschitzian continuity? This paper gives a positive answer.

arxiv-2208-09324.title: A Ptolemaic Partitioning Mechanism
arxiv-2208-09324.creator: Richard Connor
arxiv-2208-09324.description: Abstract For many years, exact metric search relied upon the property of triangle inequality to give a lower bound on uncalculated distances. Two exclusion mechanisms derive from this property, generally known as pivot exclusion and hyperplane exclusion. These mechanisms work in any proper metric space and are the basis of many metric indexing mechanisms.

arxiv-2307-08466.title: Generalizable Classification of UHF Partial Discharge Signals in Gas-Insulated HVDC Systems Using Neural Networks
arxiv-2307-08466.creator: Steffen Seitz, Thomas Götz, Christopher Lindenberg, Ronald Tetzlaff and Stephan Schlegel
arxiv-2307-08466.description: Abstract Undetected partial discharges (PDs) are a safety critical issue in high voltage (HV) gas insulated systems (GIS). While the diagnosis of PDs under AC voltage is well-established, the analysis of PDs under DC voltage remains an active research field. A key focus of these investigations is the classification of different PD sources to enable subsequent sophisticated analysis.

arxiv-2412-12745.title: Automated Penetration Testing: Formalization and Realization
arxiv-2412-12745.creator: Charilaos Skandylas, Mikael Asplund
arxiv-2412-12745.description: Abstract Recent changes in standards and regulations, driven by the increasing importance of software systems in meeting societal needs, mandate increased security testing of software systems. Penetration testing has been shown to be a reliable method to asses software system security. However, manual penetration testing is labor-intensive and requires highly skilled practitioners.

arxiv-2506-04630.title: Effects of closely spaced thresholds on line shapes with near-threshold enhancement
arxiv-2506-04630.creator: Denny Lane B. Sombillo
arxiv-2506-04630.description: Abstract Hidden-charm pentaquarks were first experimentally detected by LHCb in 2019, one of which is the exotic P c ​ c ¯ ​ ( 4312 ) + P_{c\bar{c}}(4312)^{+} state. The nature of this state remains uncertain which may be attributed to the proximity of this observed enhancement to the meson-baryon thresholds.

arxiv-2508-09819.title: Sections of Jacobian fibrations over lines
arxiv-2508-09819.creator: János Kollár and Giulia Saccà
arxiv-2508-09819.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by János Kollár and Giulia Saccà. Let | H | |H| be a linear system on a smooth surface S S . We study the cohomology classes of sections of the universal Jacobian over lines in | H | |H| . When S S is a K3 surface, the universal compactified Jacobian is a hyperkähler manifold, and we do not see how to reconcile our results with some of the steps in [BKV25].

arxiv-2508-18291.title: Design Optimized CMOS-Compatible Hybrid Silicon–MIM Waveguide Cavity for Label-Free Sensing
arxiv-2508-18291.creator: Alireza Khalilian, Hima Nikafshan Rad
arxiv-2508-18291.description: Abstract We numerically design a hybrid plasmonic–dielectric refractive-index biosensor comprising a metal–insulator–metal (MIM) bus waveguide evanescently coupled to a silicon-core resonator. The geometry is optimized with a genetic algorithm (GA) using Ansys Lumerical FDTD simulations, targeting maximal sensitivity and figure of merit while minimizing the resonance linewidth.

arxiv-2509-01476.title: Do Retrieval Augmented Language Models Know When They Don’t Know?
arxiv-2509-01476.creator: Youchao Zhou, Heyan Huang, Yicheng Liu, Rui Dai, Xinglin Wang, Xingchen Zhang, Shumin Shi, Yang Deng
arxiv-2509-01476.description: Abstract Existing Large Language Models (LLMs) occasionally generate plausible yet factually incorrect responses, known as hallucinations. Researchers are primarily using two approaches to mitigate hallucinations, namely Retrieval Augmented Language Models (RALMs) and refusal post-training. However, current research predominantly emphasizes their individual effectiveness while overlooking the evaluation of the refusal capability of RALMs.

arxiv-2602-21728.title: Explore-on-Graph: Incentivizing Autonomous Exploration of Large Language Models on Knowledge Graphs with Path-refined Reward Modeling
arxiv-2602-21728.creator: Shiqi Yan 1,2 , Yubo Chen 1 , Ruiqi Zhou 2 , Zhengxi Yao 2 , Shuai Chen 4 , Tianyi Zhang 4 , Shijie Zhang 4 , WeiQiang Zhang 1,2 , Yongfeng Huang 1,2 , Haixin Duan 1,3 , Yunqi Zhang 1 1 Zhongguancun Laboratory, Beijing, China 2 Department of Electronic Engineering, Tsinghua University, Beijing, Chin
arxiv-2602-21728.description: Abstract The reasoning process of Large Language Models (LLMs) is often plagued by hallucinations and missing facts in question-answering tasks. A promising solution is to ground LLMs’ answers in verifiable knowledge sources, such as Knowledge Graphs (KGs). Prevailing KG-enhanced methods typically constrained LLM reasoning either by enforcing rules during generation or by imitating paths from a fixed set of demonstrations.

pmc-12452399.title: Evaluating Differential Basic Resistive Skills Training Effects on Sprint, Jump, and Agility in Young Basketball Athletes
pmc-12452399.creator: Jorge Arede, Jack Wells, Mark Williams, Franc Garcia, Wolfgang Schöllhorn
pmc-12452399.description: Objectives: This study examined how differential basic resistive skills training influences basketball players’ physical performance. Methods: Seventeen young male athletes completed two weekly sessions of bodyweight strength exercises based on movement variability for 6 weeks. Countermovement jump (CMJ), sprinting, and change of direction (COD) tests were used to evaluate performance before and after the intervention and after a retention phase.

pmc-12492702.creator: Yuan Zeng, Weipeng Cai, Fei Cui, Ke Xu, Ying Huang, Wei Wang, Hui Liu, Jun Liu

pmc-12516572.description: Transdiscal screw fixation with pedicle screws at the upper level has shown promising results for lumbosacral spondylolisthesis, but there are few reports of clinical use of isolated transdiscal fixation. pmc-12689898.description: IntroductionThe concept of a dual career, which emphasizes the integration of athletic and academic pursuits, has become increasingly central to athlete development policies worldwide. pmc-12956482.creator: Pascal Demoly, Myriam Zakariya, Ignacio Dávila, Giuseppe Scibilia, Valeria Ortolani, Javier Domínguez‐Ortega, Karl‐Christian Bergmann, Philippe Gevaert, Alain Didier
pmc-12956482.description: Allergic rhinitis (AR) and asthma caused by cat dander have a highly variable prevalence across countries, which can reach 30% of the population in some regions. Cat allergens are widely distributed in the environment, making exposure nearly unavoidable, even in non‐cat‐owning households.

pmc-13439270.title: Lenalidomide ameliorates cognitive impairment via putative AChE inhibition: an in silico and in vivo study in a scopolamine-induced cognitive impairment model
pmc-13439270.creator: Salehin Sheikh, Md. Shadin, Tanzila Akter Eity, Most. Israt Jahan Oni, Mst Muslima Khatun, Raihan Chowdhury, Md. Shimul Bhuia, Mohammed Alfaifi, Faisal H. Altemani, Abdullah H. Altemani, Na’il Saleh, Muhammad Torequl Islam
pmc-13439270.description: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) causes progressive cognitive decline, and current therapies provide limited benefit. This study evaluated the neuroprotective effects of lenalidomide (LLM), a thalidomide derivative, in a scopolamine-induced mouse model of cognitive impairment, with emphasis on its acetylcholinesterase (AChE) inhibitory potential.

uslaw-usc-t15-s3703.title: 15 U.S.C. § 3703 — Definitions
uslaw-usc-t15-s3703.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t15-s3703.description: United States Code, Title 15 (Commerce And Trade); Chapter 63 (Technology Innovation). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. As used in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires, the term— (1) “Secretary” means the Secretary of Commerce. (2) “Centers” means the Cooperative Research Centers established under section 3705 or 3707 of this title. (3) “Nonprofit institution” means an organization owned and operated exclusively.

uslaw-usc-t18-s402.title: 18 U.S.C. § 402 — Contempts constituting crimes
uslaw-usc-t18-s402.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t18-s402.description: United States Code, Title 18 (Crimes And Criminal Procedure); Part I (Crimes); Chapter 21 (Contempts). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Any person, corporation or association willfully disobeying any lawful writ, process, order, rule, decree, or command of any district court of the United States, including the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court or the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court of Review established by section 103.
